sources.title: MIVUBI UI Input and Interaction Lifecycle Engineering Contract v1

facts.subject: form ownership
facts.statement: Every gameplay-relevant form must capture playerKey, connectionGeneration, arenaId/arenaGeneration where applicable, interactionGeneration, and formGeneration; the response is valid only if the ownership envelope is still current when the Promise resolves.

facts.subject: form concurrency
facts.statement: For a given player and logical form purpose, allow at most one active form owner per generation. Duplicate opens should coalesce, replace explicitly, or be rejected rather than creating competing response paths.

facts.subject: form completion
facts.statement: On form completion, re-read current authoritative gameplay state and validate player/session/arena ownership before applying the selected action. State captured when the form opened is advisory only.

facts.subject: form cancellation
facts.statement: Canceled forms, undefined selection, invalid response values, disconnects, and replaced form generations must resolve to an explicit non-action or recovery path; they must not fall through to a default gameplay action.

facts.subject: input permission ownership
facts.statement: Movement/camera/input restrictions must be owned by a scoped lease with reason, player session generation, arena generation, and restore policy. Direct fire-and-forget disable/enable calls are insufficient when multiple systems can lock the same input category.

facts.subject: overlapping control locks
facts.statement: If multiple systems may disable the same input category, restoration must use an owner set/reference count or equivalent authority model; one subsystem ending must not re-enable input while another valid lock remains.

facts.subject: input restoration
facts.statement: Disconnect, respawn, arena reset, cutscene abort, world recovery, and session-generation change must reconcile input-lock leases and restore or intentionally reapply permissions according to the current authoritative state.

facts.subject: held interaction
facts.statement: Gameplay interactions intended as one action per press must require isFirstEvent where available or implement explicit debounce/idempotency; repeated held-input events must not create duplicate purchases, revive ticks, starts, or claims.

facts.subject: interaction actor and target
facts.statement: Before applying a gameplay interaction, validate both actor and target against current session/arena/round ownership. Physical proximity or an interaction event alone is not proof that actor and target belong to the same gameplay transaction.

facts.subject: gameplay action submission
facts.statement: High-value interaction side effects such as purchase, claim, ready, start, revive completion, upgrade, or objective activation must be idempotent or guarded by an operation token so duplicate events/responses cannot apply twice.

facts.subject: UI state
facts.statement: Visible form/button state is a presentation snapshot, not authoritative gameplay state. A button being visible/enabled when the form opened does not guarantee the action remains legal when the player responds.
